lecture_summary: The lecture develops double-slit interference as evidence for light’s wave behavior, derives bright and dark fringe conditions from path difference, relates fringe angle to screen position, distinguishes exact trigonometry from small-angle formulas, and applies the same framework to diffraction gratings. The two videos below form the smallest strong, nonredundant set.

videos.title: Young's Double Slit Experiment
videos.reason: Best match for the lecture’s foundation: Young’s experiment, slit-and-screen geometry, constructive and destructive interference, and bright-fringe spacing.

videos.title: Diffraction Grating Problems - Physics
videos.reason: Adds the distinct many-slit problem type and directly covers calculations involving fringe order, diffraction angle, wavelength, and grating line density.
